howToStep1: Start a driving range session, ensuring you change to the correct club every time in the bottom left.
howToStep2: Once you have completed your session, click the clipboard in the top left:
howToStep4: Done! That's all you need to do — we take care of the rest and your session appears in UF Lab.
howToTip: You can remove any outlier or bad shots by clicking the clipboard and deleting the individual shots. UF Lab has a Hide Outliers filter too.
bagStep1: Click your player name in the Players section.
bagStep3: Match up the bag to your actual clubs.
bagStep4: Click Apply Updates to save your bag.
bagNote: Your bag setup is saved to your profile and will be applied to your future sessions automatically.
noSessionsBody: UF Lab data comes from your GSPro range sessions — select your club as you go, then hit Export to CSV on the clipboard when you finish. That's all you need to do; we take care of the rest and your shots appear here shortly after.
deleteSessionDesc: This will permanently delete the session from {{date}} and all {{count}} of its shots from the server. This can't be undone.
seeMetrics: See which metrics are improving, flat, or slipping.
sessionsInfo: Total UF Lab sessions on your account. A session is one bay visit where shots were exported from GSPro.
shotsInfo: Every shot you've captured in the UF Lab. Bucket equivalent assumes ~50 balls per range bucket.
longestCarryInfo: Furthest carry ({{unit}}). The distance the ball flew in the air, not roll.
bestClubInfo: Your best club by smash factor (ball speed ÷ club speed) shown as a percentage of the PGA Tour average for that club. Smash measures strike quality, so it rewards pure contact over raw speed. A 70-year-old can still score 95%+.
consistencyInfo: How repeatable your carry distances are, scored 0–100 (higher = tighter). We take the carry standard deviation for your three most-hit clubs, express it as a percent of each club's average, then convert to a score: 0% variation = 100, 20%+ variation = 0. Consistency is the number that actually moves with practice. Averages barely budge month to month, this does.
focusPointBody1: You're averaging a smash factor of {{avgSmash}} with your {{club}}, versus the PGA Tour average of {{tourSmash}}.
focusPointBody2: Smash factor (ball speed ÷ club speed) is the purest measure of strike quality. Closing this gap means more ball speed and carry for the exact same swing effort, no extra club speed needed.
focusPointBody3: Next session: hit a focused block with this club. Slow your tempo, aim for centre-face contact, and watch the smash number climb.
focusPointClean: Every club you've hit enough shots with is meeting or beating the PGA Tour smash benchmark. Keep grinding, a new focus point will appear as you build more data.
swingDynamicsSub: Positive = right / out-to-in for right-handers. Face-to-path shows shape tendency.
needThreeShots: Need at least 3 shots for a pattern.
compareToTargetHelp: Hit a few shots with recognised clubs (Driver, 7 Iron, PW, etc.) and we'll benchmark you against the {{label}}.
tourDescription: PGA Tour averages from Trackman. Green = tour-level, orange = close, red = big gap.
amateurDescription: Average amateur (~14 hcp) from Trackman. Green = trending toward tour, orange = around average, red = further from tour than the average golfer.
amateurNote: Higher is better for club speed, ball speed, smash and carry. For launch, spin and angle of attack, closer to the tour number is better (amateurs spin the driver too much and don't hit down enough on irons).
comparingPeriods: Comparing {{period}} vs the {{days}} days before that.
trendExplainer: Green means the metric is trending better than the previous period. Orange means little change. Red means it's slipping. Tiles need a minimum number of shots in both windows to show a trend.
consistencyProgressInfo: Are you getting more consistent? Across every club with enough shots we measure both carry standard deviation and left/right dispersion, express each as a % of the club's average carry, and convert to a 0–100 score. Higher = tighter and more repeatable.
speedProgressInfo: Are you swinging faster? For every club with enough shots we take your average ball speed and clubhead speed, then average across clubs so a change in club mix doesn't skew the number. Higher = more raw power.
driverWoodsDispersionInfo: Are your long-club shots getting more accurate? Standard deviation of left/right carry across your driver, fairway woods and hybrids. Lower = tighter, more fairways.
ironDispersionInfo: Are your irons getting more accurate? Standard deviation of left/right carry across all your irons (3i–9i). Lower = tighter approach shots.
wedgeDispersionInfo: Are your wedges getting more accurate? Standard deviation of left/right carry across all your wedges (PW, GW, SW, LW). Lower = better scoring club control.
sessionsPerWeekInfo: Are you playing enough to improve? Your average UF Lab sessions per week over the window. Practice frequency drives improvement more than any single session.
